k: It didn't fly.
src: 'It didn\'t fly.'

k: She _floated_. Briefly. With dignity. The rest is only engines, rigging, a new rudder and roughly nine thousand gold.
src: 'She _floated_. Briefly. With dignity. The rest is only engines, rigging, a new rudder and roughly nine thousand gold.'

k: But she remembers how. That's the hard part.
src: 'But she remembers how. That\'s the hard part.'

k: You'll come back for her?
src: 'You\'ll come back for her?'

k: ...Yeah, sparrow. I'll come back for her. Leaving's the thing I'm good at. Coming back is the bit I'm still learning.
src: '...Yeah, sparrow. I\'ll come back for her. Leaving\'s the thing I\'m good at. Coming back is the bit I\'m still learning.'

k: Here. From her chronometer — no use to her while she's grounded. Keeps you half a step ahead of everything. Trust me, I've needed it.
src: 'Here. From her chronometer — no use to her while she\'s grounded. Keeps you half a step ahead of everything. Trust me, I\'ve needed it.'

k: We set the singing glass in the Halcyon. She lifted — just a little. Corvin says she remembers how.
src: 'We set the singing glass in the Halcyon. She lifted — just a little. Corvin says she remembers how.'

k: Saltglass rises out of the flats like something grown, not built: white walls, blue doors, and glass everywhere — in the windows, in the streets, strung from every eave, chiming in the hot wind.
src: 'Saltglass rises out of the flats like something grown, not built: white walls, blue doors, and glass everywhere — in the windows, in the streets, strung from every eave, chiming in the hot wind.'

k: Above it all stands the Lantern, its lamp-room walled in saltglass panes. Even at noon you can see it burning.
src: 'Above it all stands the Lantern, its lamp-room walled in saltglass panes. Even at noon you can see it burning.'

k: Saltglass. Best card tables south of Aurenne, and the worst people sitting at them. I'm one of them, so I'm allowed to say that.
src: 'Saltglass. Best card tables south of Aurenne, and the worst people sitting at them. I\'m one of them, so I\'m allowed to say that.'

k: Who do you owe money to here?
src: 'Who do you owe money to here?'

k: Define "owe."
src: 'Define "owe."'

k: Listen, sparrow. While you do your holy errand, I need lift-glass for my girl. The singing kind, three good pieces. The market sells it for more than I'm worth — which, granted, isn't much.
src: 'Listen, sparrow. While you do your holy errand, I need lift-glass for my girl. The singing kind, three good pieces. The market sells it for more than I\'m worth — which, granted, isn\'t much.'

k: The cave folk dig it out of the Glass Caverns, out the east gate. Not that I'm asking.
src: 'The cave folk dig it out of the Glass Caverns, out the east gate. Not that I\'m asking.'

k: We'll help.
src: 'We\'ll help.'

k: I wasn't asking.
src: 'I wasn\'t asking.'

k: The Halcyon's Lift-Glass
src: 'The Halcyon\'s Lift-Glass'

k: Corvin needs three pieces of singing saltglass to wake his airship. It grows deep in the Glass Caverns, out Saltglass's east gate. Bring them to the wreck of the Halcyon.
src: 'Corvin needs three pieces of singing saltglass to wake his airship. It grows deep in the Glass Caverns, out Saltglass\'s east gate. Bring them to the wreck of the Halcyon.'

k: Saltglass is all white walls and wind-chimes and glass. The Lantern burns at noon. Corvin "isn't asking" for help finding lift-glass. We're helping anyway.
src: 'Saltglass is all white walls and wind-chimes and glass. The Lantern burns at noon. Corvin "isn\'t asking" for help finding lift-glass. We\'re helping anyway.'

k: The Keeper is expecting you. She's been expecting you since yesterday.
src: 'The Keeper is expecting you. She\'s been expecting you since yesterday.'

k: Don't ask me how. I stopped asking her how years ago. It's much more restful.
src: 'Don\'t ask me how. I stopped asking her how years ago. It\'s much more restful.'

k: Six children came down from the mountain with a monk who keeps apologizing to doors.
src: 'Six children came down from the mountain with a monk who keeps apologizing to doors.'

k: The Keeper took one look at them and said, "Well. I suppose I'm a grandmother now." She hasn't stopped smiling since.
src: 'The Keeper took one look at them and said, "Well. I suppose I\'m a grandmother now." She hasn\'t stopped smiling since.'

k: The Keeper lost her sight looking into the lamp. Forty years of dawns.
src: 'The Keeper lost her sight looking into the lamp. Forty years of dawns.'

k: She says she sees better now. She says most people only ever look at the light, never at what it's shining on.
src: 'She says she sees better now. She says most people only ever look at the light, never at what it\'s shining on.'

k: Saffron, salt-pepper, dried sunfruit! Nothing fresh, everything delicious.
src: 'Saffron, salt-pepper, dried sunfruit! Nothing fresh, everything delicious.'

k: You came up the Pilgrim Road? Then you missed the soldiers. Gray cloaks, forty of them, riding north last week.
src: 'You came up the Pilgrim Road? Then you missed the soldiers. Gray cloaks, forty of them, riding north last week.'

k: Didn't buy a thing. Didn't even _haggle_. That's how you know someone's dangerous.
src: 'Didn\'t buy a thing. Didn\'t even _haggle_. That\'s how you know someone\'s dangerous.'

k: The Lantern hums at dawn now. Lower than it used to. The Keeper sits up listening to it.
src: 'The Lantern hums at dawn now. Lower than it used to. The Keeper sits up listening to it.'

k: She says it's the sound of a song deciding something.
src: 'She says it\'s the sound of a song deciding something.'

k: Water! Cool water, drawn this hour from the deep well! One gold a cup, and the cup's free.
src: 'Water! Cool water, drawn this hour from the deep well! One gold a cup, and the cup\'s free.'

k: Strange thing — the Lantern's been humming at dawn this season. Low, like a cat. The Keeper's been up all night listening to it.
src: 'Strange thing — the Lantern\'s been humming at dawn this season. Low, like a cat. The Keeper\'s been up all night listening to it.'

k: I asked her what it was saying. She said, "I don't know, Dima. That's what frightens me."
src: 'I asked her what it was saying. She said, "I don\'t know, Dima. That\'s what frightens me."'

k: Forty. There are forty chimes on my eaves now.
src: 'Forty. There are forty chimes on my eaves now.'

k: I took one down this morning. Jorah's. First one I've ever taken down in eleven years.
src: 'I took one down this morning. Jorah\'s. First one I\'ve ever taken down in eleven years.'

k: My hands shook. Isn't that silly? An old woman, crying over a piece of glass on a string.
src: 'My hands shook. Isn\'t that silly? An old woman, crying over a piece of glass on a string.'

k: Forty. I like forty better than forty-one. I'd like thirty-nine even better. Bring me another miracle, child.
src: 'Forty. I like forty better than forty-one. I\'d like thirty-nine even better. Bring me another miracle, child.'

k: Every chime on my eaves is a caravan that didn't come back. Forty-one of them.
src: 'Every chime on my eaves is a caravan that didn\'t come back. Forty-one of them.'

k: The wind plays them for me, so I don't have to remember alone.
src: 'The wind plays them for me, so I don\'t have to remember alone.'

k: The newest one is Jorah's. Asha won't look at it. I don't blame her.
src: 'The newest one is Jorah\'s. Asha won\'t look at it. I don\'t blame her.'

k: Glass chimes on strings — forty of them — ringing softly in the wind. There's a gap in the row where one used to hang.
src: 'Glass chimes on strings — forty of them — ringing softly in the wind. There\'s a gap in the row where one used to hang.'

k: Glass chimes on strings — forty-one of them — ringing softly in the wind. Each one is scratched with a name.
src: 'Glass chimes on strings — forty-one of them — ringing softly in the wind. Each one is scratched with a name.'

k: Lift-glass? Ha! Everyone wants lift-glass. Sky-pirates, mostly. You have the look.
src: 'Lift-glass? Ha! Everyone wants lift-glass. Sky-pirates, mostly. You have the look.'

k: I have a _very_ trustworthy look.
src: 'I have a _very_ trustworthy look.'

k: Singing glass grows deep in the Glass Caverns, where the old Lantern-light soaked into the sand for a thousand years.
src: 'Singing glass grows deep in the Glass Caverns, where the old Lantern-light soaked into the sand for a thousand years.'

k: It hums to sunlight. And to music, they say — if you've got the right note. Old Keeper's trick. Nobody's got the right note anymore.
src: 'It hums to sunlight. And to music, they say — if you\'ve got the right note. Old Keeper\'s trick. Nobody\'s got the right note anymore.'

k: Glass is just sand that's been through something.
src: 'Glass is just sand that\'s been through something.'

k: Like people. Hotter the fire, clearer the glass. That's my philosophy, and also my sales pitch.
src: 'Like people. Hotter the fire, clearer the glass. That\'s my philosophy, and also my sales pitch.'

k: Not a raider in sight since you ran off the Jackal. My men are bored. Bored is beautiful.
src: 'Not a raider in sight since you ran off the Jackal. My men are bored. Bored is beautiful.'

k: Sarn ran? The Jackal himself? Ha! The caravans will drink to you for a month.
src: 'Sarn ran? The Jackal himself? Ha! The caravans will drink to you for a month.'

k: The council's purse, as promised. Don't spend it all in the inn. Do spend some of it in the inn. My cousin runs it.
src: 'The council\'s purse, as promised. Don\'t spend it all in the inn. Do spend some of it in the inn. My cousin runs it.'

k: Sarn's camp is in the Sunscar's south-east flats, past the glass. Red tents. Mind his slingers — they aim for the eyes.
src: 'Sarn\'s camp is in the Sunscar\'s south-east flats, past the glass. Red tents. Mind his slingers — they aim for the eyes.'

k: Pilgrims with swords. Good. I've a job, if you want it.
src: 'Pilgrims with swords. Good. I\'ve a job, if you want it.'

k: Sarn the Jackal: raider-king of the southern dunes. Camp's in the Sunscar's south-east flats. He takes a tithe from every caravan — water, coin, sometimes people.
src: 'Sarn the Jackal: raider-king of the southern dunes. Camp\'s in the Sunscar\'s south-east flats. He takes a tithe from every caravan — water, coin, sometimes people.'

k: My men can't touch him; they're needed on the walls. The town council has put up two thousand gold to see him gone.
src: 'My men can\'t touch him; they\'re needed on the walls. The town council has put up two thousand gold to see him gone.'

k: The Jackal's Tithe
src: 'The Jackal\'s Tithe'

k: Captain Idris will pay 2,000 gold to see Sarn the Jackal driven from his camp in the south-east of the Sunscar (west of Saltglass).
src: 'Captain Idris will pay 2,000 gold to see Sarn the Jackal driven from his camp in the south-east of the Sunscar (west of Saltglass).'

k: Papa's caravan is late. Mama says he's just slow.
src: 'Papa\'s caravan is late. Mama says he\'s just slow.'

k: Papa's not slow. Papa's the fastest scout on the whole salt road. So he's not late. He's just... not here yet.
src: 'Papa\'s not slow. Papa\'s the fastest scout on the whole salt road. So he\'s not late. He\'s just... not here yet.'

k: ...How long you been waiting?
src: '...How long you been waiting?'

k: Nine days. I bring my lunch.
src: 'Nine days. I bring my lunch.'

k: If you see Papa, tell him I'm waiting at the gate. He'll know which one. It's this one.
src: 'If you see Papa, tell him I\'m waiting at the gate. He\'ll know which one. It\'s this one.'

k: He's ELEVEN?! He got Kindled at ELEVEN?!
src: 'He\'s ELEVEN?! He got Kindled at ELEVEN?!'

k: I've been waiting fifteen years and eleven months! I've been _good!_
src: 'I\'ve been waiting fifteen years and eleven months! I\'ve been _good!_'

k: ...What did he get? Rogue? Okay. Okay, I feel a little better.
src: '...What did he get? Rogue? Okay. Okay, I feel a little better.'

k: Fifteen years and eleven months. ELEVEN MONTHS. And they won't let me stand in the light for thirty more days.
src: 'Fifteen years and eleven months. ELEVEN MONTHS. And they won\'t let me stand in the light for thirty more days.'

k: What if it changes its mind? What if the light was going to say Arcanist and in thirty days it says Accountant?
src: 'What if it changes its mind? What if the light was going to say Arcanist and in thirty days it says Accountant?'

k: The Queen is dead? Truly? ...My brother's caravan went into that dark eleven years ago.
src: 'The Queen is dead? Truly? ...My brother\'s caravan went into that dark eleven years ago.'
